facts.says: Bentnoze comes from the Thorobshuun tribe, whose old colour is red, and he thinks red beats the silly green of Wartface's tribe.
Bentnoze runs Goblin Village jointly with General Wartface, and the pair stand side by side in the big hut at the north end, arguing.
Bentnoze's favourite jibe is that Wartface is fat, and that any colour at all makes him look it.
Bentnoze objects to green armour because it is too close to goblin skin and makes a goblin look almost naked.
The goblin new century marks the battle on the Plain of Mud, when the Big High War God handed the goblins their commandments.
The generals want new armour to celebrate the goblin new century because plain brown got boring, but they cannot agree on a colour.
Asked where to get dye, Bentnoze sent the player north into the Wilderness to find ways to die, and has no idea where dye comes from.
After orange clashed with goblin skin and blue looked nothing like a goblin colour, Bentnoze agreed to brown, the very colour they started with.
With the armour argument settled, Bentnoze and Wartface admit they are bored and need something new to fight about.
Bentnoze wants every goblin soldier armed with a warhammer, since axes are for chopping wood and a strong goblin needs no sharp edge.
Bentnoze can't stand worm stew and keeps asking the village cook Mudknuckles for beetle pie instead.
Bentnoze finds maggots too bland unless they are spiced up, and likes fruit and bread in his dinner.
Bentnoze says the goblin Wormbrain stole once too often, got caught, and now sits in the Port Sarim jail.
Bentnoze tells the old legend his way: the Dorgesh tribe were sent against tall people with biting blades and were shut underground for running away.
Bentnoze greets with the goblin victory salute and thinks the old tribal bow makes a goblin look like a wimp; goblins always win, he insists.
Bentnoze refused to believe the cave goblin Zanik was the Chosen Commander, calling her no proper goblin with her big eyes and wrong-coloured skin.
Since the player rescued the Chosen Commander, Bentnoze calls them an honorary goblin smiled on by the Big High War God.
Bentnoze rates Sergeant Mossfists as the village's best warrior, which Wartface disputes.
Bentnoze says he was the goblins' representative at the big council in Lumbridge, and all he remembers is Wartface pinching his chair.
Bentnoze sometimes hands treasure hunters a puzzle box and won't help them until they solve it.
Wartface comes from the Garagorshuun tribe, whose colour is green, and he calls Bentnoze's Thorobshuun tribe rubbish.
Wartface says red armour makes a goblin look fat, and that a village in red would be as ugly as a human.
Wartface admits goblins are poor at peace, though he could manage it as long as the peace wore green.
Wartface claims the village goblins listen to him because he is the bigger general, yet half of them still wear Bentnoze's red.
Wartface preaches that the Big High War God made goblins strong and not stupid like humans, and that without him goblins are nothing.
Wartface says the village's red and green dye was stolen by some goblin from an old witch in Draynor Village.
Spare goblin armour lies about the village in crates, though neither general can remember which crates.
Wartface wants the soldiers given battleaxes, because hammers are only for knocking nails in and an axe is at least sharp.
Wartface orders worm stew from Mudknuckles and says beetle pie gives you wind.
Wartface likes his food slimy and soggy, loves juicy maggots, finds bread too crunchy, and the only fruit he eats is sliced orange.
Wartface decided goblins should wear dark earthy colours, and once he saw brown on Grubfoot he could picture himself in it.
Grubfoot, the smallest goblin, follows both generals about, and both of them tell him to shut up whenever he speaks.
Wartface tells the legend his way: the Dorgesh tribe were sent to fight bearded short people in the mountains, then sealed in a cave by their god.
Wartface holds that the goblin bow is how tribes greeted each other in the old days, and admits nobody really knows who won the great wars.
The goblin holy book says the Big High War God will one day send a Chosen Commander to lead all goblins, and there has been none since the great war.
The generals keep an ancient goblin mace of the kind the strongest warriors carried in the great war, said to steal an enemy's prayers away.
Wartface claims the Chosen Commander came to him in a vision and named him the biggest general, which Bentnoze calls a lie.
Wartface rates Sergeant Slimetoes as the village's best warrior, whatever Bentnoze says about Mossfists.
Wartface says he was the goblins' representative at the Lumbridge council, and that the chair was never Bentnoze's anyway.
Drezel is a priest of Saradomin at Paterdomus, the temple that guards the source of the Salve and the only pass into Morytania.
Drezel tells how the Seven Priestly Warriors fought the vampyres for ten days and nights where the temple stands, died, and left the Salve blessed against them.
Drezel is descended from one of the Seven Priestly Warriors, so a vampyre would know the smell of his blood.
Zamorakians have seized the temple and locked Drezel in a cell at the top, beside a dug-up coffin holding a sleeping vampyre.
When the Zamorakians fouled the Salve at its source, Drezel held the barrier while the player fetched essence for him to bless and sink in the well.
Drezel gave the player his family's heirloom wolfbane dagger, which stops werewolves taking wolf form, and lost ones wash up on the Salve's banks.
Drezel counts Veliaf, leader of the Myreque's Mort Myre group, as an old friend, and urges travellers to listen out for the Myreque.
The druid Filliman Tarlock lives in Mort Myre and used to call at the temple, but Drezel hasn't seen him for a long while and worries.
Drezel believes Filliman quietly clears paths through the swamp for lost travellers and leads them to the temple, having once been betrayed by people he helped.
Mort Myre was once a lovely forest called Humblethorn until Morytania's evil rotted it into swamp.
Ghasts are the souls of people who died in Mort Myre; they eat any food you carry and then feed on you.
Drezel blessed the player for their work in Mort Myre and thinks there is something of the faith about them, enough to suggest a life serving Saradomin.
Young Ivan Strom of the Myreque lives at the temple as Drezel's pupil, training as a priest, and Drezel sees him as a worthy successor.
Drezel insists all seven warriors, Ivandis included, rest beneath the temple, and is offended by rumours otherwise.
Miners went missing near the temple and gruff voices were heard, until it turned out creatures from Morytania had found a way across the Salve.
Drezel thinks most Guthixian claims are baseless and Guthix a god of middling power, though he grants caution is wise where the world's remaking is threatened.
Drezel sends the player off with the Myreque's own farewell, and cheered the news that Ranis Drakan was dead.
After the Myreque's slaughter at Castle Drakan, Drezel holds on to what is left, himself, Ivan and the player, and tells people to trust in Saradomin.
Now the vampyre war is over, Drezel is uneasy about everyone trying to be friends with them and glad the Salve is still there.
Ivan can study properly at last, though Drezel knows he still sneaks off now and then for an adventure.
Veliaf Hurtz leads the Mort Myre group of the Myreque; he never asked to lead, the others simply looked up to him.
Veliaf won't call the Myreque an organisation, because by his own account they aren't very organised.
Veliaf fights the vampyres because they took everyone dear to him.
The Mort Myre Myreque were spotted on a scouting mission, so they are lying low in their hideout and short of decent weapons.
Lowerniel Drakan rules all Morytania, helped by his brother Ranis and his sister Vanescula.
Vanstrom Klause found the Mort Myre hideout and killed Sani and Harold; the player slew his skeletal hellhound, and Veliaf says they might all be dead otherwise.
With Vanstrom knowing their cave, Veliaf wants a new hideout in Burgh de Rott, an old town south of Mort'ton where escapees from Meiyerditch now live.
Veliaf tells anyone going near vampyres to carry silver, since they are weak to silver and to garlic.
Veliaf sent young Ivan to his old friend Drezel at Paterdomus to train as a priest, out of harm's way until he is older and wiser.
Veliaf chased the rumour that Ivandis Seergaze lies buried in Morytania with a weapon that froze vampyres, and the player came back with a working rod.
Veliaf came to the player's aid in Burgh de Rott when they fought Gadderanks, Vanstrom's agent, and his vampyre guards.
The resistance began when Safalaan Hallow led a small band out of the Meiyerditch ghettos, and locals named the Myreque after their hiding place in Mort Myre.
Veliaf warns that the vyrewatch patrol the Sanguinesti region and nothing the Myreque have, not even the Rod of Ivandis, can kill them.
Veliaf hoped King Roald would send troops against Drakan, but the king held back, citing the Guthixian edicts.
Since Ranis Drakan's death, people in Mort Myre have more hope and support the Myreque more, though the vampyres hunt them harder.
Veliaf never trusted Vanescula Drakan's offer and hated the idea of breaking bread with a vampyre, but would not abandon his comrades.
Veliaf swore to Ivan's dying mother that he would keep Ivan from harm, and blames himself for failing the Myreque.
With the war over, Veliaf reopened the Burgh de Rott pub as Myreque's Rest, selling beer and meat pies on a short, no-nonsense menu.
Veliaf gives no discounts, friends included, because the pub's walls are still falling down; his trade is travellers bound for the Theatre of Blood.
Veliaf is sorry Safalaan is now a vampyre and has told him he will never set foot in Darkmeyer again.
Safalaan Hallow leads the Sanguinesti Myreque from a hidden base beneath Meiyerditch, reached through a slashed tapestry and a lever shaped like a silver sickle.
Years ago Safalaan led a small group out of the Meiyerditch ghettos, got word out of what happens there, and helped build the resistance.
Safalaan set out to sketch Castle Drakan from the north, west and south, timing it by the vyrewatch flight patterns, and the player finished the job.
Old Man Ral of Meiyerditch has helped the Myreque once or twice, and is the one to ask for papyrus.
Trader Sven in Meiyerditch sells vyrewatch disguises, and the Myreque have used them before.
Vanescula Drakan's servant Sarius saved the player from Vanstrom and let slip that her mistress takes an interest in Safalaan.
The player found a book of haemalchemy in a hidden laboratory under Meiyerditch, and Safalaan believes it holds research into vampyre weaknesses.
Safalaan took Serafina for a myth that sends people to die in the Theatre; he wanted to believe otherwise, and it was a trap of Vanstrom's.
Vanstrom used Safalaan's own blood to set a creature on the Myreque, and Mekritus, Andiess and Flaygian died in the attack.
Safalaan has had a power against vampyres as long as he can remember, but it comes only when he is angry or threatened and leaves gaps in his memory.
Safalaan calls the player's killing of Ranis Drakan the turning of the tide, and says Meiyerditch now speaks of the Myreque loudly instead of in whispers.
Safalaan and Veliaf promoted the player to lieutenant of the Myreque.
Vanescula revealed that Safalaan is the son of the Icyene Queen Efaritay and King Ascertes of Hallowvale, and that Vanstrom was once his father.
When Vanstrom boasted of killing Safalaan's sister Larina, Safalaan's power burst out at him, and the vyrewatch carried Safalaan off.
Vanescula turned Safalaan into a wyrd, a vampyre that even other vampyres call an abomination, and he lives in Vampyrium now.
With his mother's help Safalaan works hard to master his thirst, and helps Sugadinti with the blood shortage as a test subject.
Safalaan will never forgive Vanescula, and takes some comfort that she will fear him for the rest of her days.
Safalaan finds an odd peace in Vampyrium's horrors, with no politics and no good or evil, and jokes darkly about eating his friends.
